correctness.rationale: A selected clique is represented by at most one label; an unrepresented clique is dominated exactly when an adjacent clique is represented. Independence is likewise equivalent on supports, so the map preserves the minimum cardinality and all minimum configurations are precisely labelled lifts. A slide changes either one label within a selected clique or one base support vertex along a base edge while preserving shared labels. Counting these disjoint types gives the Hamming fibers, shared-label-indexed complete bipartite cross-edges, and all the displayed vertex, edge and degree formulas. Connected fibers and freely liftable base moves give the component bijection. For the metric, deleting stationary projected moves from any lifted path yields a base walk; each mismatched vertex still present at every step needs one distinct local move. Conversely, along any base walk, pay once for those persistent mismatches and set the label at each target vertex's last insertion whenever it was not persistent. This reaches the exact target labels and attains the bound, including the length-zero walk; disconnected supports give infinity. The diameter and regularity consequences follow by lifting a geodesic for the upper bound and by the degree formula. On C_n, gaps of size 2 or 3 characterize independent dominating supports, and n≥4 allows k=ceil(n/3) with d=3k−n feasible short gaps. Counting a marked starting token counts each support k times. A directed slide swaps a 2,3 or 3,2 consecutive gap pair; for each order choose its start and d−1 of the other k−2 gaps short. Division by two counts each undirected edge, including n=4,5,6 with k=2 and the stipulated zero binomials. This reconstructs the formulas in RESULT.md lines 53–61 for arbitrary graph size and positive integral fiber sizes. The frozen finite enumerator was inspected, not executed, and its reported BFS and subset checks are corroboration only.

evidence: Ordinary-cycle i-graph data give b_n and e_n without any clique multiplicities. The structural formulas add arbitrary multiplicity dependence; the metric compares all support walks using a penalty for labels never made free by departure.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Base shortest distances or a reachability reduction identify neither which labels must move nor how a walk can free a label. For a base edge with a shared occupied clique of multiplicity >1 not all pairs of lifts are adjacent, so interpreting this as ordinary clique substitution on the i-graph is not a valid implication. Cycle blowup counts are consequences of the new lift with known base data and not credited as a separate base theory.

value.rationale: This is a complete structural and metric rule for a natural host-graph operation. It gives exact nonuniform component, adjacency and enumeration data without constructing the exponentially many labelled states first. In particular it distinguishes a compulsory within-clique move from a free label change on reentry along a support walk, information not given by the component quotient. It is an exact characterization, not a claim of polynomial-time evaluation.
